doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Jazz in the house: his mother, Buffalo radio and Maynard Ferguson at Newport
summary: His mother loved jazz; the family listened to radio (WEBR, Joe Rico) and his first album was Maynard Ferguson at Newport, followed by Take Five.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: It’s a very interesting thing that you mention that movie, and people get their inspirations from interesting places.
Were you aware of that type of music before and swing.

Without a question, yeah. Our house, my mother, God rest her soul, my mother was into jazz and so we grew up on listening to jazz all the time in the house although we didn’t get the stereo really until I was about oh I’d say six or seven years old, then we finally got a stereo. Otherwise it was the little radio. And we listened to jazz all the time. And then here in Buffalo we had Sunday afternoons there was “Sinatra and Strings,” there was WEBR that had jazz all the time with Joe Rico, who was a great jazz disc jockey at that © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

time, and so we always listened to jazz in the house and as my brothers got older, because I was the baby, as everybody got older we were introduced to a little bit of R&B type jazz, you know the Lou Rawls and things like that and those kind of things. But basically the context in the house was always jazz.

Oh on the radio was everybody, but the first introductions I had, the first album I believe was Maynard Ferguson’s “Live at Newport” in ’50. And boy I can still scat all of the tunes on that record. I mean I loved that record.
